item_description: NASA's first crewed lunar landing mission, which returned astronauts and lunar samples to Earth.
item_facts: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.
The lunar module was named Eagle and the command module Columbia.
Apollo 11 landed in the Sea of Tranquility in July 1969.

item_description: An uncrewed NASA test flight of the Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft around the Moon.
item_facts: It launched in November 2022 and returned to Earth in December 2022.
The flight tested Orion systems before later crewed missions.
Artemis I traveled around the Moon without astronauts aboard.

item_description: A joint NASA, ESA and Italian Space Agency mission that studied Saturn, its rings and moons.
item_facts: Cassini orbited Saturn and sent the Huygens probe to the moon Titan.
The mission ended in 2017 when Cassini entered Saturn's atmosphere.
Cassini observed lakes and seas of liquid hydrocarbons on Titan.

item_description: India's first lunar exploration mission, which orbited the Moon and mapped its surface with scientific instruments.
item_facts: It launched aboard a PSLV rocket in October 2008.
Its payloads included instruments from India and international partners.
Data from the mission contributed evidence for water-related molecules on the lunar surface.

item_description: An Indian lunar mission that demonstrated a soft landing and robotic surface operations near the Moon's south polar region.
item_facts: The mission included a propulsion module, a lander and a rover.
Its rover carried instruments to analyze the local lunar surface.
The mission's objectives included demonstrating safe landing, rover movement and in-situ experiments.

item_description: A NASA rover exploring Gale Crater on Mars to study the planet's geology and past habitability.
item_facts: Curiosity landed on Mars in 2012.
It carries a mobile laboratory with instruments for analyzing rocks and soil.
Its findings include evidence that ancient Mars had environments capable of supporting microbial life.

item_description: A Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mission that returned samples from the near-Earth asteroid Ryugu.
item_facts: The spacecraft deployed small landers or rovers to explore Ryugu's surface.
It collected surface material and returned the sample capsule to Earth in 2020.
The mission's target, Ryugu, is a carbon-rich asteroid.

item_description: A space observatory that has studied the universe across ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared wavelengths.
item_facts: Hubble launched aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery in 1990.
Astronauts serviced and upgraded it during multiple Space Shuttle missions.
Its observations have contributed to research on galaxies, stars and the expansion of the universe.

item_description: A space observatory designed primarily for infrared astronomy, studying objects from the early universe to nearby planetary systems.
item_facts: Webb is a partnership among NASA, ESA and the Canadian Space Agency.
It operates near the Sun-Earth second Lagrange point, about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
Its segmented primary mirror unfolds after launch to form an approximately 6.5-meter mirror.

item_description: A Soviet spacecraft that became the first human-made object to reach the surface of the Moon.
item_facts: It impacted the lunar surface in September 1959.
The mission carried instruments to study radiation and the lunar environment.
Luna 2 did not make a controlled soft landing; it struck the Moon.

item_description: The Mars Orbiter Mission was India's first interplanetary mission and studied Mars from orbit.
item_facts: ISRO launched the spacecraft in November 2013.
It entered Mars orbit in September 2014.
Its scientific payloads studied Martian surface features and atmosphere.

item_description: A NASA mission that delivered a lander and the Sojourner rover to the Martian surface in 1997.
item_facts: Sojourner was the first rover to operate on another planet.
The mission landed in Ares Vallis, a region in Mars's northern hemisphere.
Pathfinder used airbags to help cushion its landing.

item_description: A NASA spacecraft that performed the first close-up exploration of Pluto and later flew past a Kuiper Belt object.
item_facts: New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015.
It later explored Arrokoth, a small object in the Kuiper Belt.
The spacecraft launched in 2006 and uses a radioisotope thermoelectric generator for power.

item_description: A NASA sample-return mission that collected material from the near-Earth asteroid Bennu and brought it back to Earth.
item_facts: The sample capsule landed in Utah in September 2023.
Bennu is a carbon-rich asteroid whose material can preserve clues about the early solar system.
After delivering its sample, the spacecraft continued on an extended mission renamed OSIRIS-APEX.

item_description: A NASA mission designed to study the Sun's outer atmosphere and the solar wind at close range.
item_facts: The spacecraft uses a heat shield to protect its instruments during close solar passes.
It studies the corona and the flow of charged particles known as the solar wind.
Its trajectory uses repeated Venus flybys to alter its orbit around the Sun.

item_description: A NASA rover exploring Jezero Crater on Mars, studying its geology and collecting samples for possible future return to Earth.
item_facts: Perseverance landed on Mars in February 2021.
It carries the Ingenuity helicopter, which completed powered flights in the Martian atmosphere.
The rover collects and seals rock and regolith samples in tubes.

item_description: A European Space Agency mission that orbited comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko and deployed the Philae lander.
item_facts: Rosetta was the first spacecraft to orbit a comet.
Philae made the first soft landing on a comet nucleus.
The mission ended in 2016 with Rosetta's controlled descent to the comet.

item_description: The first artificial satellite to orbit Earth, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957.
item_facts: Sputnik 1 transmitted radio signals that could be detected from Earth.
The satellite was a polished metal sphere with four external radio antennas.
Its launch marked the beginning of the Space Age and the Space Race.

item_description: A NASA spacecraft that explored Jupiter and Saturn before traveling into interstellar space.
item_facts: Voyager 1 launched in 1977 and flew past Jupiter and Saturn.
NASA determined that it crossed into interstellar space in 2012.
The spacecraft carries a Golden Record containing sounds and images from Earth.

item_description: A NASA spacecraft that visited all four giant planets and continues its journey beyond the heliosphere.
item_facts: Voyager 2 is the only spacecraft to have visited Uranus and Neptune.
It launched in 1977, before Voyager 1, despite reaching Jupiter later.
Like its twin, it carries a Golden Record with sounds and images from Earth.
